messages:
Maya: FYI: After 2.1.3 driver rollout, noticed p95 token latency up ~25% for seqlen=1024 on A100 pool. Flamegraph + profile here: https://ci.redwood.local/artifacts/2770001234/flame.svg :thinking:
Kevin: Hmm. Is this kernel-selection or batching? Did kernel-decider change? Can you paste the perf command + env?
Maya: repro run:
```
RUNTIME_DRIVER=2.1.3 ./bench --model redwood/ggml-13b --seq-len 1024 --batch 1 --profile=flame
```
Flame shows a big spike in `select_kernel_for_block` and repeated `kv_cache.invalidate` calls.
Susan: If kv_cache.invalidate is hot it usually means keys aren't stable across runtime restarts or kernel swaps. Did the driver change key format?
Maya: I grepped — driver 2.1.3 added `kernel_hint` append to key when `auto_kernel` enabled. That means old keys don't match, we end up re-populating cache per request.
Arjun: That's rough. Quick idea: make autotuner write a compatibility header + epoch to the persisted key namespace so we can tolerate transitional keys.
Susan: Proposal (key recipe):
```
key = f"{model_hash}:{seq_bin}:{kernel_id}:{kernel_epoch}:{quant_flag}"
```
kernel_epoch increments only on *incompatible* kernel ABI changes, avoiding churn for minor tunables.
Kevin: Also add a short debounce on invalidation ops (10s) and a coalescing queue — saves a ton under bursty restarts. Add CI perf test to assert invalidations/sec < X.
Maya: I'll run the perf harness with `--seq-profile=record` and the debounce patch. If we still see p95 regressions, we should fallback routing to the previous kernel variant for existing cache keys.
deploy-bot: Rollout 2.1.3 -> production scheduled for 2026-03-19 03:00 UTC. Canary window: 30m. :rocket:
Susan: For persistence: keep backward-compatible reader that tries v2 key then v1 (legacy). If v2 present, migrate lazily on access.
Maya: Great. I'll push a small PR with key schema + debounce + canary gating. Will post CI numbers here. Thanks!
Kevin: Thanks — tag me @Maya when the PR is up. :thumbsup:
